To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ethanol‐induced expression of proinflammatory and profibrotic cytokines is counteracted by the inhibitor of cytochrome P‐450 2E, chlormetiazole.
chronic alcohol exposure causes an increase in the zonated hepatic expression of cytokines, which is inhibited by the CYP2E‐inhibitor CMZ.
ethanol‐mediated induction of CYP2 E1 is associated with an enhanced expression of cytokines, and that the cytochrome 2E1‐inhibitor CMZ counteracts this effect of ethanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the zonal expression of cytokines and the effect of chronic alcohol consumption on their expression.
the zonated cytokine expression in the rat liver.
the zonated distribution of cytokines and the influence of ethanol and the CYP2E inhibitor CMZ on cytokine expression in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zonated cytokine expression in the liver is a result of a complex interplay of various factors and mechanisms, including the zonated distribution of the CYP2E enzyme.
CYP2E‐inducible oxidative stress may play a key role in the induction of proinflammatory and fibrogenic cytokines in the pathogenesis and progression of ALD.
the zonated distribution of the cytokines in rat livers is not affected by alcohol, whereas the expression of TGFβ1 is enhanced by alcohol and is inhibited by CMZ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic ethanol exposure causes an increase of CYP2 E1 expression, and that CYP2E 1 is responsible for increased cytokine expression, which in turn is associated with liver injury.
the expression of several cytokine genes is zonated in rat liver and that ethanol‐induced CYP2E expression and activity is associated with increased cytokine expression.
the zonated cytokine expression in the rat liver is affected by chronic alcohol consumption and the cytochromes P450‐2E1 inhibitor CMZ.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CYP2E is not only a marker of alcohol abuse, it is a major player in the pathogenesis and progression of alcoholic liver disease, as it induces the release of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, such as IL‐6, TNF‐α and TGF‐β, and thus contributes to the development of alcoholic liver injury.
chronic alcohol consumption increases the expression of cytokines such as TNF‐α, TGF‐β, IL‐1β, and IL‐6 in the liver.
